name: Killimy
questions: Can you send the floor plan with room sizes? Which rooms sit next to the ground-floor master suite, and could one of the two living rooms serve as a sitting room for older parents, with its own door to the garden?

The brochure says both 'circa 1 acre' and 'over three quarters of an acre'. Can you send the folio map? Is the boundary dog-proof all round, especially along the R419 frontage, and is the rear paddock fenced separately?

What is the heating system and the BER's exact kWh/m²/yr figure, when was the house built, and was the first floor converted later (with certificates of compliance for the conversion and the Velux rooms)?
Is water from the mains or a private well, and is drainage a septic tank or a treatment unit? How old is it, and is it registered?

BuyerIQ shows one critical finding (locked) and 10 planning applications within 1 km, one an active build. Has a radon test been done, and are any of those applications on the sites next door or the field opposite?

ai.why: A 243 m², five-bed, four-bathroom dormer bungalow at €499k with a ground-floor master suite and two living rooms, about 10 minutes from Portarlington's Dublin trains and 12–15 from Portlaoise's ED. Held back by its spot in a ribbon of one-off houses on the R419, with neighbours about 35–40 m away on both sides, and by no floor plan or photos to judge the layout and finish. Held at 3.0: a ribbon of 8–10 houses on the R419 with neighbours ~35–40 m away and no photos or floor plan yet to confirm character — close to the Monmore pattern, lifted by the ground-floor parents' zone, two living rooms and the ED ~12 min away.

electricity.detail: Likely mains; not stated, but the house sits in a row of homes on the R419 at the edge of Emo village.

water.detail: Unknown; not stated in the Daft or MyHome text, and the MyHome Features list is empty. A house on the edge of Emo may be on mains or a group scheme. Ask.

sewer.detail: Likely septic; not stated, but a one-off house outside the village core is usually on a septic tank or treatment unit. Ask its age and registration.

internet.detail: Likely fibre; not stated in the listing and BuyerIQ's broadband data is locked. NBI names Emo's rural townlands in its Portarlington deployment area, and Laois's NBI rollout reached closeout in Sept 2026. Check nbi.ie by Eircode.

groundFloorBedroom.detail: The listing puts three double bedrooms on the ground floor, the master with its own dressing room and en-suite, beside two living rooms, the kitchen/dining room and a guest WC; with no floor plan, how separate that suite is from the family rooms is unconfirmed.

bedsNote: Three doubles on the ground floor (master with dressing room and en-suite); upstairs a large master suite with a full dressing room and en-suite shower, and a second bedroom with its own en-suite
heating: Not stated; BER B2 (100–125 kWh/m²/yr band, exact figure not published)
tagline: A 243 m² five-bed dormer bungalow with a ground-floor master suite, two living rooms and a rear paddock with stabling, on about 0.75–1 acre on the R419 at the edge of Emo, Co. Laois.

pros.text: 243 m² with two living rooms for six
pros.detail: Five bedrooms, a large kitchen/dining room, a 'substantial' living room and a second separate living room, plus a utility room, per the listing; €2,050/m².

pros.text: Ground-floor master suite for the parents
pros.detail: The ground-floor master has its own dressing room and en-suite, with two more doubles and a family bathroom on the same floor, so the parents need no stairs.

pros.text: Four bathrooms plus a guest WC, on both floors
pros.detail: Ground floor: master en-suite, family bathroom and guest WC; first floor: an en-suite to each of the two bedrooms, so each sleeping floor has its own.
Portarlington station is about 6.2 km straight-line: about 19 weekday commuter trains to Heuston (about 1h05) plus InterCity stops; the M7 is about 3 km south.
Midland Regional Hospital Portlaoise is about 7.4 km straight-line; its 24-hour ED takes adults and children, with a new paediatric extension opened in 2026.

pros.text: €499k, just inside the budget, BER B2
pros.detail: Stamp duty about €4,990; B2 means 100–125 kWh/m²/yr, and the listing notes green-mortgage eligibility.

pros.text: Paddock, stabling and garage on 0.75–1 acre
pros.detail: A rear paddock with concrete stabling, a large detached concrete garage, a deck and a covered al-fresco area, behind electric gates with mature trees.

pros.text: Emo village and Emo Court on the doorstep
pros.detail: Emo's centre is about 0.7 km, Emo Mixed NS about 0.8 km and Emo Court's grounds about 2 km; Emo has a pub and church but no shop was found.

cons.text: A ribbon of houses on the R419, neighbours 35–40 m away
cons.detail: On Esri satellite imagery the pinned house is one of about 8–10 one-off houses within 100 m along the east side of the R419, about 20 m back from the road, with neighbours roughly 35–40 m to the north and south; open fields lie across the road and behind. BuyerIQ flags R419 traffic noise as high priority.

cons.text: No floor plan, room sizes or viewable photos yet
cons.detail: Neither Daft nor MyHome shows a plan or room dimensions, and MyHome has no photos, so the separation of the ground-floor suite, the size of the common rooms and the finish are unconfirmed.
A dormer bungalow with Velux rooms upstairs; the listing calls it 'charming' and 'beautifully presented', but its age, style and floor finishes are unverified.
The listing says both 'circa 1 acre' and 'over three quarters of an acre'; a rough satellite estimate is about 0.3–0.4 ha (0.8–0.9 ac), below the 1-acre target.

cons.text: Water, drainage, heating and broadband not stated
cons.detail: MyHome's Features list is empty and neither listing names the heating, water supply, drainage or broadband.

cons.text: No shop in Emo; school quality unknown
cons.detail: The nearest supermarkets are in Portlaoise (about 8.5 km) and Mountmellick (about 7 km); Emo Mixed NS's 2016 inspection report couldn't be read, and St Mary's CBS Portlaoise sent about 68–71% to third level in older tables.

cons.text: One locked critical finding on BuyerIQ
cons.detail: BuyerIQ lists one critical and two high-priority findings (one is R419 noise) plus 10 planning applications within 1 km, one an active build; Laois addresses often flag radon. Ask for a radon test.
